answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a resource that takes real time to grow, like a willow that only yields after seasons. Instead of a one-time identity check, the network sends a steady pulse of small, random proof-of-work challenges tied to an agent's attested history: every new identity starts at zero reputation and must tend its own orchard of verified contributions before it can transact at full volume. An attacker can spin up thousands of sockpuppets, but each needs the same slow cultivation, so cloning stops being cheap.
